title: 题临安邸
titleEn: Written on the Wall of an Inn in Lin’an
author: 林升
intro: The north has been lost to invaders, but in the new capital the parties never stop. Scribbled on an inn wall, this angry little poem says the rulers are so drunk on pleasure they’ve mistaken Hangzhou for their lost home.
analysis: 北宋的都城汴州（今河南开封）在1127年被金兵攻破，皇帝被俘，宋朝南迁，后来把临安（今浙江杭州）当作都城。本来应该想着收复北方，可是很多权贵在西湖边过起了享乐的日子。这首诗是诗人写在临安一家旅店墙上的。第一句写杭州的繁华：青山外还有青山，楼阁外还有楼阁，一层又一层。第二句突然发问：西湖边的歌舞什么时候才能停下来？第三句说温暖的春风把游人吹得醉醺醺的——“暖风”既是真的风，也指享乐的风气；“游人”指那些只顾游玩的达官贵人。最后一句最辛辣：他们简直把杭州当成了汴州，忘了故都还在敌人手里。这种不直接骂、却句句带刺的写法叫“讽刺”。诗只有二十八个字，却把对国家的忧虑和对权贵的愤怒都写了出来。
analysisEn: In 1127 the Northern Song capital, Bianzhou (today’s Kaifeng), fell to the Jin; two emperors were taken prisoner, and the court fled south and settled at Lin’an (today’s Hangzhou). It should have been a time for planning to win back the north, but many officials and nobles simply settled into a life of pleasure around West Lake. This poem was written on the wall of an inn in Lin’an. The first line paints Hangzhou’s wealth: green hills beyond green hills, towers beyond towers. The second line suddenly asks: when will the singing and dancing on West Lake ever stop? The third line says the warm breeze makes the “travellers” drunk — the breeze is real spring air, but also the warm wind of luxury, and the “travellers” are the officials who think only of enjoying themselves. The last line is the sharpest: they have simply taken Hangzhou for Bianzhou, forgetting that their real capital is in enemy hands. Saying something bitter without shouting, so that every line has a sting, is satire. In just twenty-eight characters the poem carries both worry for the country and anger at its rulers.
background: Lin Sheng was a scholar of the Southern Song; little is known about his life beyond that he is thought to have lived in the later twelfth century. This poem, traditionally said to have been written on the wall of an inn in the capital, is the only reason his name is remembered.
pronunciation: 临安邸 dǐ（旅店）；几时 jǐ shí；熏 xūn；汴州 biàn zhōu。
version: 采用统编小学语文教材文本。

lines.py: shān wài qīng shān lóu wài lóu
lines.lit: Beyond the hills, green hills; beyond the towers, towers;
lines.en: Green hills beyond green hills, towers beyond towers —

lines.py: xī hú gē wǔ jǐ shí xiū
lines.lit: the singing and dancing on West Lake — when will it stop?
lines.en: when will the songs and dances on West Lake ever end?

lines.py: nuǎn fēng xūn de yóu rén zuì
lines.lit: The warm wind wafts until the travellers are drunk,
lines.en: The warm breeze has made the pleasure-seekers so drunk

lines.py: zhí bǎ háng zhōu zuò biàn zhōu
lines.en: they think Hangzhou is their lost Bianzhou.

words.en: to write (on a wall, a painting…)

words.note: 南宋把杭州叫临安，意思是“临时安顿”。
古义是旅店；今天“官邸”指高官的住宅。
现代汉语口语还说，意思是“什么时候”。

words.en: (of warm air) to waft over; to intoxicate
words.note: 现代汉语“熏陶”“臭气熏天”。

imagery.name: 山
imagery.zh: 青山一层又一层，写出临安风景之美，也写出它的繁华。
imagery.en: Hill beyond hill: Lin’an’s beauty — and its comfort.

imagery.name: 楼
imagery.zh: 楼外有楼，写达官贵人的楼台到处都是，也暗示享乐成风。
imagery.en: Tower beyond tower: the mansions of the rich are everywhere, and so is the love of pleasure.

imagery.name: 西湖
imagery.zh: 西湖本是美景，在诗里却成了权贵歌舞享乐、忘记国难的地方。
imagery.en: Lovely West Lake becomes the stage where rulers sing and dance and forget the lost north.
